newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends up but continues to lag behind N.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends up but continues to lag behind N.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures were little moved in the afternoon despite skyrocketing New York arabica futures and prices ended Thursday with their morning gains.
Traders said the bullish sentiment in New York on supply tightness failed to prevail in London where robustas are in good supply.
New York's arbitrage to London continued to gap much wider and by late Thursday, it stood at new record high of $1.78 basis May.
"There are a lot of robustas aroud, why should London follow New York?" said one trader.
Thursday's first notice day saw some 791 lots were tendered against LIFFE's May contract and traders said a lot more notices were in the pipeline.
By the close, July stood $41 up at $1,659 a tonne while spot May rose $36 to $1,574.
Overall volume was 4,692 lots, with July outrights and July/Sept switches leading the actives.
New York's July futures hit a new contract high of 221.25 cents a lb. By 1650 GMT, it was up a hefty 10.10 cents on the day at 220.50.
More gains were likely with funds, speculators and roasters were seen steeping up panic buying.
"The situation is explosive. Nobody dare sell the market," said one trader. "It's a bull market. you can't go against the winds."
Traders said overnight comments by Merrill Lynch that the coming Colombian crop could be delayed could have set the tone for the latest rally. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
